title: DAMPyF: a Python implementation of the DAMPF method for the simulation of open-system dynamics
authors: Nicola Lorenzoni, Susana F. Huelga, Martin B. Plenio
abstract: DAMPyF is an open-source Python implementation of the dissipation-assisted matrix product factorization (DAMPF) method, a tensor-network-based approach for the numerically exact simulation of finite-dimensional quantum systems coupled to bosonic environments. The method relies on a pseudomode representation of structured reservoirs and a matrix-product-state representation of the density matrix of the extended system, comprising the system and the pseudomodes. DAMPyF currently provides two workflows. First, it supports excitation energy-transfer dynamics within the single-system-excitation manifold, in which a system excitation is propagated in time. Second, it provides a high-level workflow tailored to molecular spectroscopy, in which the system levels represent electronic states and optical coherences are propagated for the subsequent computation of linear spectra, including absorption and circular dichroism. This paper describes the physical model, the DAMPF algorithm, the user-facing code structure, installation and execution, input and output formats, and minimal examples.
summary: This paper introduces DAMPyF, an open-source Python tool implementing the DAMPF method to simulate open quantum dynamics. It allows for numerically exact simulation of system-environment coupling using tensor networks (MPS) applied to pseudomode representations. The tool is versatile, supporting both general energy transfer and specialized molecular spectroscopy calculations.
main_problem: The simulation of open quantum systems where a finite system interacts with an environment exhibiting memory effects, requiring non-perturbative treatment.
main_result: Introduction of DAMPyF, an open-source Python implementation enabling numerically exact simulations for complex dynamics like energy transfer and molecular spectroscopy.
method: The Dissipation-Assisted Matrix Product Factorization (DAMPF) method is used to represent the extended density matrix ($ho_{se}$) via a tensor network approach (MPS formalism).
model_or_system: The system involves a finite quantum system coupled to an environment modeled by structured reservoirs, often described by generalized spin-boson models. Dynamics are governed by the GKSL master equation.
key_observables: Reduced system density matrix ($ho_s(t)$), linear absorption spectra ($A(\omega)$), and circular dichroism spectra ($	ext{CD}(\omega)$).
important_parameters: Pseudomode bond dimension ($\chi$), time step ($\Delta t$), thermal energy ($k_BT$), and system coupling strengths.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the pseudomode representation of structured reservoirs, which assumes Gaussianity to maintain numerically exact reduced system dynamics. Trotter decomposition introduces an error $O(\Delta t^2)$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 conceptually illustrates partitioning the environment into a non-Markovian core and Markovian remainder; Figure 2 graphically details the DAMPF decomposition of $ho_{se}$ using MPSs.
paper_structure: The paper describes the physical model, the DAMPF algorithm derivation, the user-facing code structure (including installation/execution), input/output formats, and provides minimal working examples for various applications.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses state-of-the-art simulation techniques for open quantum systems, which is a major focus area in modern AMO physics, especially concerning light-matter interactions and energy transport.
